checks: Explicit opt-in, publisher identity and atomic read/write grants; stale administrator edits cannot erase grants.
Concurrent identical registration is idempotent; key conflicts, foreign ownership and source/method injection are rejected.
Metadata edits preserve identity/data contract, enforce revision and survive repeated startup publication.
Auto-granted credentials ingest and query immediately; queued and processed data both block deletion.
Empty deletion removes definition/grants, retains audit, supports retries and reserves the stable key.
Coverage and a durable usage marker block deletion even after data is removed by retention or cleanup.
Event metrics can self-publish dataset schema and ingest; schema conflicts roll back metric and grants.
Concurrent ingestion versus deletion has one winner; accepted records never lose their definition.
Startup retries never restore removed grants; pre-granted dimension scopes are preserved.
Disabling management takes effect without revoking data access; explicit read/write grants never confer ownership.
Human definitions are not silently adopted and revoked credentials cannot self-publish.
Grant-budget exhaustion rejects registration atomically without changing metrics or integration revision.
